basis: Enlargement of the renal parenchyma defines the condition.
Superficial fascia and subcutaneous tissue belong to the dermatologic axis; other organs vary across subtypes.
Latent Treponema pallidum infection; no common organ damage defines the early latent stage.
Germ cell tumors originate in reproductive gonadal tissue, rather than hormone-producing endocrine tissue.
Isolated congenital nail absence and dystrophy; distal phalangeal abnormalities occur in only 5-29%.
Vascular malformations, limb overgrowth and cutaneous capillary lesions define KTS; gastrointestinal vascular lesions cause bleeding in 30-79%. Embolism and cellulitis are separate complications.
Dilated cardiomyopathy with severe ventricular dysfunction; hydrops and effusions reflect cardiac failure. Developmental delay in 1/2 lacks established direct neurologic injury.
Orbital bony margin agenesis and malformations of eyelids and lacrimal drainage define the syndrome.
Pontocerebellar and other brain malformations with severe developmental impairment; neutropenia and thrombocytopenia each occur in 2/9, below 30%.
Developmental and epileptic encephalopathy defines the disease. Visual impairment in 1/1 has no established ocular localization; feeding difficulty does not establish gut damage.
Severe bone fragility and deformity with dentinogenesis imperfecta are defining features; scleral color does not establish ocular dysfunction.
Molecular subtype of an atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor arising in the central nervous system.
GCM2-related primary hyperparathyroidism; osteopenia occurs in 3/19 and kidney stones in 4/19, both below 30%. Stones are also separately diagnosed.
Inflammation of the superficial cornea; an infectious or autoimmune mechanism is not established for the umbrella concept.
Structural lesion of the carotid arterial intima; associated ischemic stroke is a separately diagnosed complication.
Congenital hypoparathyroidism and intellectual disability define SSS; dental/enamel defects occur in 30-79%. Growth delay alone does not establish bone injury; ocular defects are usually 5-29%.
Congenital cardiac and extensive skeletal abnormalities with intellectual disability characterize the syndrome; ocular findings lack frequencies sufficient for an additional axis.
Congenital heart defects, intellectual disability and generalized skin abnormalities define the syndrome, each reported at 30-79%; short stature alone does not establish skeletal damage.
Type B brachydactyly features distal phalangeal hypoplasia or absence with hypoplastic or absent nails; other reported abnormalities lack evidence of common involvement.
Wilms tumor arising in the adult kidney; metastatic sites are not intrinsic organ involvement.
Inherited glucose transport defect; renal, neurologic and intestinal manifestations belong to different subtypes and do not apply across the umbrella.
Established steroid-induced glaucoma damages the eye and optic nerve; treatment causation does not remove the defining organ of this disease.
ATP1A2-related hemiplegic migraine is a neurologic disorder; nausea and transient visual symptoms do not establish gastrointestinal or ocular damage.
Ocular albinism and severe brain abnormalities define it; hearing impairment and hypochromic anemia each occur in 80-99%. Skin hypopigmentation and immune abnormalities omitted at the four-axis cap.
Brachydactyly and arterial hypertension occur in nearly all patients; later stroke is a separately diagnosed complication and is not added as neurologic involvement.
